proposedTopics.title: Storage gas
proposedTopics.description: Persistent storage access is among the EVM's most expensive work, so many gas wins come from touching fewer slots, avoiding redundant loads and stores, and choosing layouts that match access patterns.

proposedTopics.title: Calldata & memory gas
proposedTopics.description: Calldata is read-only input supplied by the caller, while memory is mutable per-call scratch space. Calldata bytes affect intrinsic transaction gas and expanding memory charges execution gas according to the highest word accessed.

proposedTopics.title: Control-flow gas
proposedTopics.description: Loops and conditionals can magnify repeated work. Optimize measured compiler output: short-circuit expensive branches, remove only proven redundancy, cache stable values when the compiler does not, and return once the result is known.

proposedTopics.title: Packing variables into slots
proposedTopics.description: The compiler places state variables contiguously and packs adjacent value types smaller than 32 bytes when they fit. Packing can reduce the number of slots touched when fields are read or written together, but updating one packed value requires a read-modify-write and can cost more than an unpacked value. Optimize the layout for actual access patterns, not slot count alone.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/SlotPacking.sol — compare two equivalent layouts, then reorder fields used together so the measured write path touches fewer slots. Done when: forge test passes, storageLayout confirms the slot mapping, and forge snapshot records the before/after gas delta under the same compiler settings.

requirements.purpose: Apply Solidity's exact packing rules and account for packed-value read-modify-write costs

proposedTopics.title: Warm vs cold access (EIP-2929)
proposedTopics.description: EIP-2929 charges the first access to a storage key or covered account absent from the transaction-wide accessed sets at the cold rate and later accesses at the warm rate: SLOAD is 2100 cold versus 100 warm, while covered account-access opcodes charge 2600 cold versus 100 warm. The sender, destination, precompiles, and EIP-2930 access-list entries begin warm; access-list entries have their own intrinsic charges.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/WarmCold.sol — measure first and repeated accesses to one storage key and one external account, with and without an EIP-2930 access list. Done when: tests preserve behavior and the trace plus transaction gas accounting explains the cold charge, warm charge, and access-list intrinsic charge separately.

proposedTopics.title: Minimizing SLOAD and SSTORE
proposedTopics.description: SLOAD pricing depends on warm or cold access, while SSTORE metering depends on the slot's original, current, and new values plus any cold-access surcharge and refund. Accumulating in a local and committing once can remove repeated storage operations, but a no-op guard is worthwhile only when its saved store outweighs the added branch and load on real call distributions.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/StorageWrites.sol — change an accumulator loop from repeated storage updates to one final commit, and benchmark a guarded no-op write against the unguarded form. Done when: forge test passes, the trace shows one final SSTORE, and snapshots document both changed-value and same-value paths.

proposedTopics.title: Caching storage in memory
proposedTopics.description: Copying a stable storage value into a local can let later uses avoid repeated SLOADs. The local may live on the stack or in memory depending on compiler output, and caching is unsafe across code that can change the underlying state, including relevant external-call reentrancy.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/CacheStorage.sol — compare repeated state-variable reads with one local snapshot, including a variant containing an external call. Done when: behavior tests pass, compiler output shows the actual load count, and snapshots quantify the delta without allowing a stale cache across state-changing code.

proposedTopics.title: constant vs immutable for gas
proposedTopics.description: A constant's expression is replaced where it is used, while an immutable is assigned during construction and its value is copied into reserved locations in runtime code. Neither occupies a normal storage slot, so reads avoid SLOAD; constants suit compile-time expressions and immutables suit deploy-time values.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/Immutable.sol — convert a deploy-time fixed storage configuration value into an immutable and compare it with a true compile-time constant. Done when: tests pass, storageLayout and opcode output show no normal storage slot or SLOAD, and snapshots include deployment size and read-path deltas.

proposedTopics.title: SSTORE refunds (EIP-3529)
proposedTopics.description: EIP-3529 set the storage-clear refund schedule to 4800 gas, removed the SELFDESTRUCT refund, and limits applied refunds to one fifth of gas used. Whether deleting a slot realizes all 4800 depends on the transaction's refund counter and cap; clearing state still consumes gas before the refund is applied.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/Refunds.sol — clear one and then several originally nonzero slots, recording gross gas, the refund counter, the one-fifth cap, and net gas. Done when: tests pass and the measured receipts match a hand calculation for both an uncapped and cap-limited case.

proposedTopics.title: Transient storage for gas (EIP-1153)
proposedTopics.description: EIP-1153 defines TSTORE and TLOAD at 100 gas each for transaction-scoped state discarded after the transaction. Transient state is shared across a contract's frames under the same ownership rules as persistent storage, so a lock must still be explicitly cleared before returning if later calls in the same transaction should proceed.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/TransientLock.sol — implement and test a transient-storage reentrancy guard, including two sequential calls in one transaction and a reverting inner call. Done when: the guard blocks reentry, unlocks on normal return, leaves no durable state, and a trace accounts for each 100-gas TLOAD/TSTORE.

proposedTopics.title: Packing structs and enums
proposedTopics.description: Struct members start a new slot and then follow the same contiguous packing rules as state variables; items after a struct also begin a new slot. Current Solidity enums have at most 256 members and occupy one byte in storage. Reordering members can reduce slots, but packed partial updates add read-modify-write work.

Done when: tests preserve field values, the optimized layout uses fewer slots for each array or mapping element, and snapshots record whole-struct and single-field update costs.

proposedTopics.title: calldata over memory
proposedTopics.description: Calldata is non-modifiable call input. For read-only reference-type parameters, keeping data in calldata can avoid a memory copy, but the exact generated operations and savings depend on ABI decoding, access patterns, compiler version, optimizer settings, and whether downstream code requires memory.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/CalldataArgs.sol — compare equivalent external functions taking a read-only dynamic argument in memory and calldata across several input sizes. Done when: tests match, compiler output identifies any copy avoided, and snapshots record the size-dependent delta under pinned compiler settings.

proposedTopics.title: Custom errors over require strings
proposedTopics.description: Custom errors ABI-encode a four-byte selector plus typed arguments and are usually cheaper than string descriptions. They can reduce deployed bytecode and revert-data work, but exact savings depend on the string, arguments, compiler, and optimizer. Solidity supports custom errors with revert and, in current versions, require.

Done when: tests assert exact revert data and snapshots compare deployment size plus successful and reverting paths under pinned compiler settings.

proposedTopics.title: Shrinking calldata
proposedTopics.description: EIP-2028's standard calldata accounting assigns 16 gas per nonzero byte and 4 per zero byte, while EIP-7623 applies a 10-gas-per-token floor that can make data-heavy transactions effectively pay 40 and 10 respectively. Standard ABI arguments still occupy 32-byte words even when their Solidity integer types are narrow, so meaningful shrinking requires fewer arguments or an explicitly compact, unambiguous encoding whose on-chain decode cost and calldata floor are included in the comparison.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/ShrinkCalldata.sol — compare standard ABI arguments with one explicitly compact bytes payload over representative values and input counts. Done when: round-trip tests pass and receipt accounting separates the 21000 base, EIP-2028 standard calldata charge, execution/decode gas, and EIP-7623 total-cost floor to identify the break-even point.

proposedTopics.title: Avoiding memory expansion
proposedTopics.description: EVM memory cost for a high-water mark of a 32-byte words is Cmem(a) = 3a + floor(a² / 512); expansion charges only the difference from the previous high-water mark. Reaching the same final size incrementally does not repeatedly repay prior expansion, so optimization means reducing the highest word touched or avoiding repeated allocation and copying—not merely preallocating the same final range.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/MemoryExpansion.sol — compare dense writes, a sparse high-offset write, and repeated allocations that copy data while reaching controlled high-water marks. Done when: tests pass and measured expansion deltas match Cmem(new) - Cmem(old), separating expansion from copy and allocation work.

proposedTopics.title: abi.encodePacked encoding cost
proposedTopics.description: abi.encodePacked concatenates direct arguments without standard ABI padding and omits lengths for dynamic values. It can reduce encoded size, but exact gas is compiler- and workload-dependent; with two dynamic arguments the encoding is ambiguous and can create hash collisions. Prefer abi.encode unless a bounded fixed layout makes packed encoding unambiguous and measured savings matter.

Done when: tests prove the fixed layout is unambiguous, reproduce the dynamic collision, and snapshots record encoded lengths and gas under pinned compiler settings.

proposedTopics.title: Short-circuit ordering
proposedTopics.description: Logical && and || short-circuit, so putting a cheap, selective condition first can skip later work. Reordering is semantics-preserving only when evaluation order is not observable: operands must not rely on side effects, reverts, or state changes from the original order.

Done when: behavior tests pass and traces plus snapshots show which paths evaluate the SLOAD.

proposedTopics.title: Unchecked increments
proposedTopics.description: Solidity arithmetic reverts on overflow by default; an unchecked block restores wrapping arithmetic. A loop increment can be unchecked only when its bound and control flow prove that increment cannot wrap. Any gas delta is compiler- and optimizer-dependent and must be measured rather than assumed.
proposedTopics.aiContext: Build: solve gas/UncheckedLoop.sol — compare checked and unchecked increments in a bounded loop and document the proof that wrapping is unreachable. Done when: boundary tests cover zero and maximum permitted lengths, compiler output shows the removed check if any, and snapshots record the measured delta.

proposedTopics.title: ++i over i++
proposedTopics.description: Postfix i++ evaluates to the old value and prefix ++i to the new value, but when that result is unused a current optimizer can produce equivalent code. Do not claim a gas win from syntax alone: inspect optimized output and benchmark the pinned compiler; choose the clearer form when they are identical.

proposedTopics.title: Caching array length
proposedTopics.description: A loop condition that reads a storage array's length may cause repeated warm SLOADs; caching a length that cannot change during the loop can remove them. It is incorrect when the body can change the length, and current compiler optimization must be inspected because it may already hoist some invariant reads.

Done when: tests cover both stable and changing lengths and traces plus snapshots show whether repeated length loads remain.

proposedTopics.title: Removing redundant checks
proposedTopics.description: A check is removable only when the same invariant is enforced on every path by the language, an earlier dominating condition, or a trusted boundary. Solidity address types do not imply nonzero, and external calls can invalidate earlier state assumptions; preserve load-bearing checks and prove redundancy with negative tests.

Done when: positive, overflow, and authorization tests pass and compiler output plus snapshots show whether the redundant branch remains.

proposedTopics.title: Early return
proposedTopics.description: Returning once a result is known can skip later reads and computation on that path. The optimization depends on path frequency and compiler output, and an early return must not bypass required state changes, cleanup, authorization, or invariant checks.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How does declaration order of small state variables affect gas, and why?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Adjacent value types smaller than 32 bytes pack when they fit, so fields used together can require fewer slot accesses. Pitfall: updating only one packed field needs a read-modify-write, and interleaving a full-word field can force another slot.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a two-field storage layout (a uint128 and a uint128) that the compiler packs into one slot.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: uint128 a; uint128 b; // declared consecutively, both occupy slot 0 at offsets 0 and 16. Verify with the compiler's storageLayout output rather than inferring opcode count from layout alone.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve the storage-packing gas puzzle in the RareSkills gas-puzzles repo.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Reorder fields so hot ones pack into a single slot; measure with forge snapshot until under target.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Under EIP-2929, what do cold and warm access cost for a storage slot and for an account?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Slot: cold SLOAD 2100, warm 100. Covered account access: cold 2600, warm 100. An access is cold only when absent from the transaction-wide accessed sets; the sender, destination, precompiles, and EIP-2930 entries start warm, with access-list entries charged intrinsically.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a snippet that reads the same storage variable twice so only the first read pays cold cost.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: uint256 x = s; // cold if this key was not prewarmed or touched ... uint256 y = s; // the key is warm afterward. An optimizing compiler may eliminate the second SLOAD, so confirm the intended accesses in a trace.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve a warm/cold access gas puzzle from the RareSkills gas-puzzles repo.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Reorder or dedupe accesses so repeat touches are warm (100) not cold (2100/2600); snapshot under target.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why can SLOAD be quoted with warm/cold prices while SSTORE needs original, current, and new values?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: EIP-2929 sets SLOAD to 100 warm or 2100 cold. EIP-2200 branches SSTORE metering on original/current/new values, with later fork rules adding cold surcharges and changing refunds; there is no single universal update price.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a loop that accumulates into a local and writes storage once at the end.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: uint256 sum; for (uint256 i; i < n; ++i) { sum += a[i]; } total = sum; // one SSTORE instead of one per iteration.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why is caching a storage variable in a local worth it even for warm reads?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: A local snapshot can let the optimizer reuse a value instead of issuing another SLOAD. Exact placement and savings depend on generated code. Pitfall: relevant state can change across an external call, making a cache stale.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a loop condition and body that read a state variable `count` only once.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: uint256 c = count; for (uint256 i; i < c; ++i) { ... } // read `count` into c once, use c throughout.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How do `constant` and `immutable` each avoid an SLOAD, and when do you use which?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: A constant expression is substituted at each use; an immutable is assigned during construction and copied into reserved runtime-code locations. Use constant for compile-time values and immutable for deploy-time ones. Neither uses a normal storage slot.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write an immutable owner set at deploy and a constant fee.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: address public immutable owner; uint256 public constant FEE = 100; constructor() { owner = msg.sender; } // neither read costs an SLOAD.

proposedPrompts.promptText: What does clearing a slot refund, and what did EIP-3529 change?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Clearing a slot that was originally nonzero to zero adds the 4800 storage-clear refund. EIP-3529 capped applied refunds at 20% of gas used and removed the SELFDESTRUCT refund; other dirty-slot reset cases follow EIP-2200's separate accounting.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a function that frees a slot to earn a refund.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: delete balances[user]; // if the slot was nonzero at transaction start, setting it to zero adds the 4800 clear refund, subject to the 20%-of-used cap.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why is a TSTORE/TLOAD reentrancy lock cheaper than an SSTORE-based one?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: TSTORE and TLOAD each cost 100 gas and transaction-scoped state is discarded at transaction end. Pitfall: clear a lock before returning if later calls in the same transaction must proceed; never use it for durable state.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a reentrancy guard using transient storage (tstore/tload).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: assembly { if tload(0) { revert(0,0) } tstore(0,1) } _; assembly { tstore(0,0) } // each transient opcode costs 100 gas; explicit unlock permits later same-transaction calls.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How do you order struct members to minimize slots, and where do enums fit?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Order adjacent value types so their byte widths fit each slot, then verify compiler storageLayout. Current Solidity enums occupy one byte. Pitfall: fewer slots can make a single packed-field update more expensive.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a struct that packs an address, a uint96, and a bool into two slots.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: struct P { address owner; uint96 amount; bool active; } // owner(20)+amount(12)=32 → slot 0; active → slot 1.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why is a read-only external array argument cheaper as calldata than memory?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: calldata keeps read-only input in its original data area, while a memory parameter needs an independent mutable representation. The exact copy and savings depend on ABI decoding and generated code; inspect the pinned compiler output.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write an external function signature that reads a bytes argument without copying it.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: function f(bytes calldata data) external { ... } // `calldata` avoids the memory copy a `bytes memory` param would force.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How do custom errors save gas versus require strings?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: A custom error ABI-encodes a 4-byte selector plus typed arguments instead of a string description. It is usually cheaper, but deployment and revert-path savings vary with the error payload and compiler settings.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Rewrite `require(x > 0, "zero")` using a custom error.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: error Zero(); ... if (x == 0) revert Zero(); // current Solidity also supports require(x > 0, Zero()).

proposedPrompts.promptText: What are the intrinsic gas costs of calldata bytes, and how do you lower them?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: EIP-2028's standard charge is 16 gas per nonzero byte and 4 per zero byte. EIP-7623 can instead make the total-cost floor bind at an effective 40/10 for data-heavy transactions. Narrow Solidity integers still occupy 32-byte standard ABI words; include decoding and the floor when comparing compact encodings.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a call that packs two uint8 args into one bytes32 instead of two padded words.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: bytes32 packed = bytes32(uint256(a) << 8 | uint256(b)); // one 32-byte word decoded on-chain vs two padded args.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How is memory priced, and why does a large buffer get expensive fast?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: For a high-water mark of a words, Cmem(a) = 3a + floor(a²/512); expansion charges Cmem(new) - Cmem(old). Incremental growth to the same final word does not repay old expansion, though repeated allocation/copying can add work.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a loop that reuses one preallocated memory buffer instead of allocating each iteration.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: bytes memory buf = new bytes(32); for (uint256 i; i < n; ++i) { /* overwrite buf */ } // allocate once, reuse.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When can abi.encodePacked produce fewer bytes than abi.encode, and when is it unsafe?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Packed mode omits standard padding for direct arguments and lengths for dynamic values, often producing fewer bytes. Gas still must be measured. Two dynamic values make boundaries ambiguous and can collide; prefer abi.encode unless the layout is provably unambiguous.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a collision-safe keccak256 over two fixed-width values using encodePacked.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint256(a), address(b))); // fixed-width operands make boundaries unambiguous; benchmark before claiming a gas saving over abi.encode.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How does operand order in `&&`/`||` save gas?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: && stops at the first false, || at the first true, so put the cheapest/most-decisive operand first (e.g. a calldata compare before a cold SLOAD). Pitfall: only reorder side-effect-free operands, or you change behavior.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Assume `admin` is immutable; reorder `require(store[id].active && msg.sender == admin)` to gate the storage read.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: require(msg.sender == admin && store[id].active); // the side-effect-free immutable comparison runs first, so the storage read only runs if it passes.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why does `unchecked { ++i; }` save gas, and when is it safe?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Checked arithmetic panics on overflow; unchecked restores wrapping behavior. It is safe only when bounds and control flow prove the increment cannot wrap. Any gas delta depends on compiler and optimizer output.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a for-loop whose counter increment is unchecked.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: for (uint256 i; i < n;) { /* body */ unchecked { ++i; } } // i < n < 2^256, so the increment can't overflow.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When the expression result is unused, can you assume `++i` is cheaper than `i++`?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: No. Prefix returns the new value and postfix the old one, but an optimizer can discard the unused result and emit equivalent code. Compare optimized IR, bytecode, and a benchmark for the pinned compiler.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the cheapest loop-counter increment idiom for an unused return value.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: unchecked { ++i; } // valid only after proving the bound prevents wrap. Prefix is conventional, but verify output rather than claiming it always beats postfix.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Why cache `arr.length` before a loop over a storage array?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: The condition may re-read a storage array's length each iteration; caching a stable length can reduce that to one load. Inspect optimized output because the compiler may already hoist it, and never cache when the body can change the length.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a loop over a storage array `items` that reads its length only once.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: uint256 len = items.length; for (uint256 i; i < len;) { ... unchecked { ++i; } }

proposedPrompts.promptText: What makes a check safe to remove, and give an example of a redundant one.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Remove only checks whose condition is already guaranteed — e.g. SafeMath on top of 0.8's built-in overflow checks, or re-validating an input a modifier already checked. Pitfall: deleting a load-bearing check to save gas is how exploits get introduced — prove redundancy first.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Rewrite `unchecked`-safe addition that drops a redundant SafeMath-style check under solc 0.8.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: uint256 c = a + b; // 0.8 already reverts on overflow — no need for a manual `require(c >= a)`.

proposedPrompts.promptText: How does returning early lower average gas?
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Returning as soon as the result is known skips the remaining storage reads/loops/computation on the common path. Pitfall: ensure the early path still runs any required state updates before returning.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a function that returns immediately when the amount is zero, before any storage work.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: function f(uint256 amt) external { if (amt == 0) return; /* expensive storage work only for amt > 0 */ }
